create-pdf.formula:
characters per line ≈ usable width ÷ (font size × 0.5)
lines per page = usable height ÷ (font size × 1.45)
image scale = min(usable width ÷ image width, usable height ÷ image height)
howTo: Choose the Text tab for a written document, or the Images tab for a photo PDF.
For text: type a title and author (optional), paste your text, and set the font size and margins.
For images: add your photos — each becomes one full page, in the order you choose.
Pick the page size: A4 or US Letter.
Click “Create PDF” and download the finished document.
keyFacts: The text builder wraps words by measuring each line with the real Helvetica font metrics — no guessing.
Pagination is automatic: when the next line would cross the bottom margin, a new page starts.
A4 is 595.28 × 841.89 points and US Letter is 612 × 792 points (72 points = 1 inch).
Your title and author are written into the PDF's document metadata, visible in any reader's properties panel.
Each image gets its own page, centered and scaled to fit with its aspect ratio preserved.

Tables, columns and complex layouts are not supported — plain flowing text only.
Very long documents (hundreds of pages) may be slow on low-end devices.

create-pdf.workedExample:
A 2,000-character note on A4 (595.28 × 841.89 pt), 12 pt font, 72 pt margins:
usable width = 595.28 − 144 = 451.28 pt → about 75 characters per line
usable height = 841.89 − 144 = 697.89 pt → 697.89 ÷ 16.8 ≈ 41 lines per page
2,000 ÷ 75 ≈ 27 lines — fits on a single page.
